title: Multitenant sparse hypercube for ad-hoc slice analytics
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: ad-hoc exploration in Console (per-tenant, per-route, per-model, by time-window and feature-set) produces expensive wide scans and high egress cost. Current curated marts cover common slices but struggle with low-cardinality dimensions enumerated in many combinations. We need a flexible, storage-efficient canonical layer that supports fast ad-hoc slicing without exploding table counts or precomputations.

Proposal: design and implement a multitenant 'sparse hypercube' abstraction: a compact canonical table format that stores only non-empty dimension cells using a wide-column / sparse-vector encoding and light-weight inverted indexes for high-cardinality dimensions. The layer will be accompanied by a set of materialized shards for hot dimensions (tenant, route, model, day) and on-demand delta materialization for infrequent slices. Query planner hints and runtime bloom filters will prune partitions to achieve low-latency interactive queries.

Goals: reduce average query scan bytes for ad-hoc Console queries by >= 6x vs current canonical wide table; enable sub-second/low-second queries for typical dashboard pivots; maintain canonical lineage and data contracts used by Console and cost attribution pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Analytics and Data Infra: includes schema, partitioning, index choices, retention/cost model
Prototype of sparse encoding + inverted index implemented in ETL with automated unit tests
Benchmarks show >=6x reduction in scan bytes and >=2x improvement in median query latency for representative ad-hoc pivots
Materialized shard strategy implemented for tenant/day/route and hooked into nightly refresh; documented fallback to full-scan when necessary
Query routing integrates bloom-filter pruning and returns correct results for canonical queries (end-to-end data contract tests pass)
Migration plan for existing consumers with backwards-compatible views and deprecation timeline documented
design_decisions: Encoding: store sparse dimension vector as JSONB-like compressed map in Parquet rather than exploding columns to keep schema stable
Indexing: maintain per-dimension inverted index tables with compressed posting lists (columnar) for high-cardinality dims; use Bloom filters in partition metadata to speed pruning
Sharding: materialize tenant/day/route shards for hot traffic and rely on delta-materialization for ad-hoc slices older than 7 days
Storage format: Parquet with dictionary and ZSTD compression for cost-efficiency; small-file compaction jobs scheduled daily
Query surface: expose as canonical view + planner hints; do not require consumers to change query semantics initially
implementation_steps: Write design doc and run review with Analytics/Infra (owner: Avery)
Prototype ETL that produces sparse hypercube parquet files and inverted index tables (owner: Marco)
Integrate bloom-filter metadata into partition manifest and test pruning logic in Presto/Trino query layer
Build nightly materializer for tenant/day/route shards; add compaction and retention enforcement
Create canonical view that joins hypercube with inverted indexes and materialized shards; add compatibility tests
Run performance benchmarks and adjust encoding/indexing parameters
Rollout to staging dashboards, gather feedback, then production rollout with migration docs
risks_mitigation: Risk: inverted index growth can increase metadata overhead — mitigation: implement compressed posting lists and TTL for low-usage dimensions
Risk: query planner support for bloom filters could be uneven — mitigation: provide fallback hint that forces shard-only scan when pruning unreliable
Risk: consumers rely on column-exists semantics — mitigation: maintain compatibility view with null fill for missing dims during migration
Risk: small-file overhead from many sparse parquet files — mitigation: schedule regular compaction and monitor file counts
